notes: Nothing posts until a person sets status to approved. See docs/linkedin/playbook.md section 10. page_reply is the in-character first comment, posted by hand within the hour.

items.text:
Linked Beats is now on LinkedIn.

We have spent the last several quarters aligning on whether to have a page. Today we are pleased to share that alignment has been reached.

You can expect regular updates on our work, our people, and our commitment to the kind of work our people do.

Grateful.

Synergy, Host
Linked Beats
items.page_reply: Strategy: Excited to see where this narrative takes us. Or framework. We've agreed it's both.

items.text:
Reflecting on a week of making knowledge more accessible across the organization.

On Tuesday I corrected the sharing permissions on our onboarding folder. Eleven people now have the link. Four of them have opened it.

A small change. But a reminder that access is not a destination. It is a setting.

Operations, Linked Beats

Our newest Partnerships hire, Kevin, completed his first week.

He finished the new-hire checklist, met each team lead, and was added to the welcome channel, the culture channel, and the channel for questions about channels.

He has one outstanding access request, which we are treating as an opportunity.

Welcome, Kevin. The folder is coming.

People & Culture, Linked Beats

I used ChatGPT to draft a guide to our shared Google Drive.

It produced four pages. I removed two. The remaining two explain where the folders are and who to ask for access.

Who to ask is still being confirmed.

Sometimes the most important output of a tool is a clearer picture of the question.

Keys, Enablement
Linked Beats

A look inside Internal Distribution.

Every morning, one member of our team moves the day's deliverables from the print room to the floor. No announcement. No recap. No follow-up thread.

We asked if there was anything we could do to support the work.

The work continued.

Linked Beats
items.page_reply: Synergy: Let's make sure this gets captured in the Q4 narrative.

items.text:
Humbled to be recognized at Alignment Summit 2026.

I will not say much about the award itself. The category was broad, the field was strong, and attendance was a component.

What I will remember is the conversations. Specifically, the one about whether our Q4 narrative is a narrative or a framework. We have agreed it is both.

Grateful to the organizers, to my team, and to the many people who sat near me.

Strategy, Linked Beats
items.page_reply: Linda: We received one in 2019. It's in the spreadsheet.

items.text:
From this week's Tuesday alignment.

Keys: I used ChatGPT to draft a guide to our shared Drive.
People & Culture: Love this.
Kevin: Does the guide say how to get access?
Keys: It says to ask your manager.
Kevin: Who is my manager?
Synergy: Let's take that offline.

Minutes available on request.

Linked Beats
items.page_reply: Operations: Minutes are in the folder.

items.text:
Encouraged by the visibility our latest post is generating.

Our social media intern published Thursday's campaign post and reported 1,140 impressions by Monday. We asked what an impression is. The explanation was clear, which is more than we had before.

Arjun asked how many of them were people. We are looking into it.

Proud of this team.

Synergy, Host
Linked Beats
items.page_reply: Strategy: Let's zoom out. What's the broader impressions narrative?

items.text:
This week, four members of our team made space to invest in their growth.

Each completed the five-lesson Professional Development Program and received a certificate. Each posted the certificate. Each certificate was congratulated by the other three.

Development is a cycle.

The program is open to everyone.

Synthia, Corporate Training
Linked Beats

article.title: Professional Development Program
article.description: Five lessons. One certificate. Learn the genre one notch of the dial at a time.

items.page_reply: Synthia: A short training on how to complete the training is now available.

items.text:
My mom turned 68 on Saturday. Here is what it taught me about sales.

Relationships matter. Showing up matters. I brought the cake, and I would do it again.

Nobody bought anything, and that was not the point. But I did notice that the people who stayed longest were the ones who felt heard.

Something to carry into Q4.

Operations, Linked Beats
items.page_reply: Synergy: Let's capture that as a learning.

items.text:
Three weeks ago I asked for access to the Partnerships folder. On Friday, the request was declined.

I am grateful.

Not because I have the folder. I do not. But because the process worked exactly as designed, and I now understand the design.

In other news, I have sent follow-up emails to everyone I met at Alignment Summit. Two have replied. One asked for access to the folder.

Kevin, Partnerships
Linked Beats
items.page_reply: People & Culture: We see you, Kevin. A working group has been formed.

items.text:
We updated the website.

The registration link on the Programs page had pointed to the 2024 form since 2024. It now points to the current form. I had flagged this in a spreadsheet, which I still have.

The launch recap meeting is Thursday. Three teams will present.

Linda, Governance
Linked Beats
items.page_reply: Synergy: Huge cross-functional effort. Thank you all.

items.text:
I cried after a 1:1 today. And that is okay.

It was a good conversation. We talked about belonging, about the welcome channel, and about why Kevin still cannot open the folder. I did not have an answer. I said so.

Then we formed a working group.

Vulnerability is a leadership skill. So is scheduling.

People & Culture, Linked Beats
items.page_reply: Arjun: Does the working group have the folder?

items.text:
Optimizing.

Our Deliverables function produced forty seconds of output this week. We asked for a summary.

This is the summary.

Linked Beats
items.page_reply: Operations: Printed copies available on request.
